From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ramos <carlos@streamlytics.io>, SRE Team <sre@streamlytics.io>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark run results — summary for MAP (attached CSV + notes)

Carlos / Priya — thanks for provisioning the tenant and keys. We executed the two windows and ran the planned concurrency sweep. Attaching the raw CSV (benchmark-results-summary-0309.csv). Below is a concise summary for the MAP deliverable and recommended next steps.

Summary (representative, single-sequence mix):
- TTFT (time to first token): median 78 ms, 95th 185 ms
- Latency (response end) p50 / p95 by concurrency:
  - concurrency 8: p50 110 ms, p95 260 ms
  - concurrency 32: p50 140 ms, p95 390 ms
  - concurrency 128: p50 330 ms, p95 820 ms (tail impact from queuing spikes)
- Sustained throughput:
  - 32 concurrent streams: 295 req/s observed (passes MAP threshold)
  - 128 concurrent streams: peak 980 req/s but with elevated p95; recommend autoscaling at 64->128 boundary
- Stability: 2 short spikes during the first window correlated with noisy neighbor activity; second window after quantization tweak (8-bit) reduced mean latency by ~12% at 32 concurrency, p95 improved ~8%
- Observability notes: token-level breakdown (attached CSV columns) shows batching efficiency drops after 64 concurrent streams — likely kernel scheduling pressure on the instance profile we used.

Pass/fail vs MAP criteria:
- p50 < 200ms: PASS across tested concurrencies
- p95 < 500ms: PASS at 8 and 32 concurrency, MARGINAL at 128 (820ms) — recommend mitigation (autoscale + slightly larger GPU profile)
- TTFT < 120ms: PASS
- sustained throughput >= 250 req/s at 32 concurrency: PASS (295 req/s)

Recommended next actions to include in MAP before close:
1) For contract: provision Dedicated capacity sized for steady-state 32-concurrency at the recommended instance (A100x2-equivalent) with autoscale to 128 for burst.
2) Engineering follow-up: kernel/kernel-queue tuning and targeted evictions to address p95 at 128+ concurrency.
3) Business: adjust SLA clause to include a defined autoscale behavior and warm KV cache requirements for cold-start-sensitive flows.

Attachments: benchmark-results-summary-0309.csv (raw), redwood-map-benchmarking-runbook-20260308.pdf (runbook), load-window-schedule.ics

If this aligns with you, we'll update the MAP doc and push an updated MAP milestone that pins the close target to 2026-03-19 (assuming Dedicated commitment).

Best,
